poster_title: Generalist Reward Models: Found Inside Large Language Models
authors: Yi-Chen Li, Tian Xu, Yang Yu, Xuqin Zhang, Xiong-Hui Chen, Zhongxiang Ling, Ningjing Chao, Lei Yuan, Zhi-Hua Zhou

content: RLHF is the main paradigm for aligning LLMs with human values.
Training RMs on human preferences is costly and difficult to scale.
Heuristic methods for internal reward extraction lack theoretical guarantees.
High-quality reward signals are essential for LLM alignment.
External RMs are expensive and not scalable.
Internal reward extraction methods lack rigorous theoretical foundations.
Discover endogenous reward within LLMs trained via next-token prediction.
Prove theoretical equivalence to offline IRL reward functions.
Extract reward function from LLM logits using inverse soft Bellman operator.
Validate theoretical findings on various LLMs.
Compare performance with LLM-as-a-judge and explicit RM training.
Surpasses explicitly trained RMs on expensive human-labeled data.
Fine-tuning with endogenous reward improves policy error bound.
Endogenous reward can replace reward modeling stage in LLM alignment.
Proposes a more efficient and theoretically grounded paradigm.
Suggests viable alternative to costly human preference datasets.
